::: {#sol-linear-quadratic}

| $n$ | 10 | 50 | 100 | 200 | 1000 |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $100 n$ | 1000 | 5000 | 10000 | 20000 | 100000 |
| $n^2$ | 100 | 2500 | 10000 | 40000 | 1000000 |

The second algorithm takes fewer steps when $n < 100$, and the two take the same number at $n = 100$.
For every $n > 100$, $n^2 = n \cdot n > 100 n$, so the first algorithm takes fewer steps,
and the ratio $n^2 / (100 n) = n / 100$ grows without bound.
The factor 100 decides which is better on small inputs;
the powers $n$ and $n^2$ decide which is better on large ones.

:::
